events: The Assembly called
An ordinance of the Lords and Commons calls divines to advise Parliament on the liturgy, discipline and government of the Church of England.
The first sitting
The Assembly meets in Henry VII’s Chapel in Westminster Abbey. William Twisse preaches and is prolocutor.
The Solemn League and Covenant
The Commons and the divines swear the Covenant with Scotland at St Margaret’s in Westminster. Scottish commissioners come to sit with the Assembly.
From the Articles to church government
The Assembly has revised fifteen of the Thirty-Nine Articles. Parliament now turns it to the government and discipline of the church.
An Apologeticall Narration
The five Dissenting Brethren among the divines appeal to Parliament for congregational liberty. The long debate on church government begins.
The Directory for Public Worship
Parliament puts the Assembly’s Directory in place of the Book of Common Prayer.
Twisse dies
William Twisse was the first prolocutor. Charles Herle succeeds him.
The Confession of Faith
It is presented to the House of Commons. The Scripture proofs follow on 29 April 1647.
Received in Scotland
The General Assembly of the Church of Scotland approves the Confession.
The Larger Catechism
It is presented to Parliament. The Shorter Catechism follows on 25 November.
The last numbered session
Session 1163. The divines go on meeting as a committee to examine ministers.

names.bio: John Lightfoot (b. 1602, Stoke-upon-Trent, Staffordshire; d. 1675, Ely) was an English biblical scholar and the foremost Christian Hebraist of his generation. Educated at Christ's College, Cambridge, and long rector at Ashley in Staffordshire, he devoted himself to rabbinic literature under the conviction that the Talmud and midrashim, whatever their polemical burden, preserve the idiom, geography, and institutions that illuminate the New Testament.
